requirements.title: Procedures may be defined by means other than Fortran
requirements.definition: A procedure may be defined by means other than Fortran.

requirements.title: Non-Fortran procedure interfaces may be specified by interface bodies or procedure declarations
requirements.definition: The interface of a procedure defined by means other than Fortran may be specified by an interface body or by a procedure declaration statement.

pending.interface-body-route-for-nonfortran-proc: Mixed Fortran/C plan uses an interface body for FUNCTION cf_add1(x) BIND(C, NAME='cf_add1') RESULT(r) with INTEGER(C_INT), VALUE :: x and INTEGER(C_INT) :: r, linked to C int cf_add1(int x){return x+1;}; cf_add1(41_C_INT) changes result sentinel -42_C_INT to exact 42_C_INT.
pending.procedure-declaration-route-for-nonfortr: Mixed Fortran/C plan declares ABSTRACT INTERFACE; FUNCTION iface(x) BIND(C) RESULT(r) with IMPORT C_INT, INTEGER(C_INT), VALUE :: x, and INTEGER(C_INT) :: r; END, then declares PROCEDURE(iface), BIND(C, NAME='cf_add1') :: p and links to C int cf_add1(int x){return x+1;}. This procedure declaration form is admitted by R1512-R1514 because BIND(C, NAME=...) is a proc-attr-spec, satisfies C1515 by using a previously declared abstract interface, satisfies C1520 by having exactly one nonpointer nondummy proc-decl with NAME=, satisfies C1521 because iface has a proc-language-binding-spec, and relies on 18.10 for C interoperability; p(41_C_INT) changes result sentinel -42_C_INT to exact 42_C_INT.

requirements.title: References to non-Fortran procedures use external-subprogram reference semantics
requirements.definition: A reference to a procedure defined by means other than Fortran is made as though it were defined by an external subprogram.

pending.nonfortran-reference-external-subprogram: Mixed Fortran/C plan references C int cf_add1(int x){return x+1;} from Fortran exactly as an external function through an interface FUNCTION cf_add1(x) BIND(C, NAME='cf_add1') RESULT(r); INTEGER(C_INT), VALUE :: x; INTEGER(C_INT) :: r. Calling cf_add1(41_C_INT) must yield exact 42_C_INT, proving the as-though-external reference semantics in Fortran-visible behavior.

requirements.title: Invoked non-Fortran procedures that continue execution return to their Fortran caller
requirements.definition: A non-Fortran procedure invoked by a Fortran procedure and not terminating execution returns to its caller.

pending.nonfortran-normal-return-to-caller: Mixed Fortran/C plan provides C void cf_touch(int *x){*x = 17;} and Fortran interface SUBROUTINE cf_touch(x) BIND(C, NAME='cf_touch') with INTEGER(C_INT) :: x. The Fortran caller initializes x=-17_C_INT and after CALL cf_touch(x) executes the next Fortran statement token=99_C_INT; expect x==17_C_INT and token==99_C_INT, proving the C procedure returned to its caller.

requirements.title: A proc-language-binding-spec makes the procedure interoperable
requirements.definition: A procedure whose interface has a proc-language-binding-spec is interoperable as described in 18.10.
